key_insight: Surfactant kinetics matter mainly when dynamic surface tension differs during impact: Surfynol 465 enables greater wetting and final coverage than Triton X-100 or SDS, especially on rough surfaces.
engineering_relevance: For surface-coating, printing, and spray processes on rough substrates, choosing a surfactant with faster effective adsorption can improve spread area and wetting reliability.
method: Experimental drop-impact tests on rough surfaces
Compare Triton X-100, SDS, and Surfynol 465
Vary concentration relative to CMC and Weber number
evidence_signal: The abstract reports nearly identical coverage evolution below CMC, but pronounced differences at 2×CMC, with Surfynol 465 consistently producing larger coverage areas across roughness levels.
watch_item: Results depend on surfactant kinetics, impact speed, and surface roughness, so conclusions may not transfer directly to other liquids or substrate textures.
paper_title: Effect of surfactant kinetics on the wetting following the drop impact onto rough surfaces
